items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: There was what they called the Freddie James tap dancing. That was known as close rhythm... there were three of them that were inspired by Freddie James

ctx.x: Well, would you say that most tap dancers were limited in their scope as dancers? They only had one particular routine, and they'd just do it over and over and really didn't expand?

No. They were required to do a certain amount of minutes, which is 5-1/2 minutes. They would have to have a dance routine, or tap dance appearance, as it was known then. That approximated 5-1/2 minutes of program, see. So there was all kinds of tap dancing. There was what they called the Freddie James tap dancing. That was known as close rhythm, you see. Just like when you're closing an envelope on a letter, or something like that.
I'm not sure I know what you mean. Could you explain that a little bit further?
